title: Capacity Forecast (Draft) — Dedicated Fleet — 2026 H1
body:
Last updated: 2026-02-10 (J. Pierce)
Status: working draft for 2026 H1 plan; aligns with Dedicated tiering proposal (Standard/Plus/Premium) and shape standardization.

---

1) Summary (exec-friendly)

H1 2026 Dedicated capacity plan is driven by (a) committed tier guarantees (throughput floor), (b) regional GPU supply constraints, and (c) headroom targets by tier to avoid SLO misses during customer load spikes and fleet incidents.

Base-case outcome (recommended):
- Add net +44 H100 GPUs and +96 L40S GPUs in H1, mostly in us-east + eu-central; keep A100 fleet flat to down slightly (planned retirements) while migrating Standard/Plus customers off A100 where margin/SLO benefit.
- Hold Premium deployments to H100-only shapes (8x H100) except explicit exception process.
- Maintain a dedicated “burst reserve” pool per region sized to ~8–12% of committed tier capacity (H100) and ~10–15% for L40S (more variance in perf by workload).

Primary risk: eu-central H100 lead time (8–12 weeks) + shipment uncertainty, and expected Q2 uptick in regulated workloads (Premium) pulling demand forward.

Decision asks (Infra + Finance + Product):
- Confirm headroom targets by tier for 2026 H1 (see §4) and whether we treat “burst reserve” as separate from headroom.
- Approve procurement plan for incremental H100 (us-east, eu-central) by 2026-03-01 to land by April/May.

---

2) Definitions / planning conventions

Units:
- “GPU” = physical GPU device (H100/A100/L40S).
- “Node” = 8-GPU server (unless otherwise stated).
- “Committed capacity” = GPUs allocated to customer deployments (Dedicated pools), excluding warm spares.

Tier planning assumptions (for capacity math; customer-facing language is elsewhere):
- Premium: highest throughput floor + strictest admission control; requires warm spare posture.
- Plus: moderate burst + stronger failover posture than Standard.
- Standard: best-effort burst; relies more heavily on shared burst reserve and scheduling.

Utilization targets (sustained, excluding planned maintenance windows):
- Premium committed GPU utilization target: 62% (lower to preserve SLO under variance)
- Plus committed GPU utilization target: 68%
- Standard committed GPU utilization target: 72%

Notes:
- These utilization targets are not the same as “headroom”; they’re a derived planning knob that bakes in variability (sequence length mix, streaming overhead, batchability, cache hit rate).
- We still model explicit headroom/warm spares separately.

---

Base-case net adds over H1:
- H100: +44 GPUs total (us-east +20, us-west +8, eu-central +16)
- A100: -48 GPUs total (retirements, move to non-Dedicated or decommission)
- L40S: +96 GPUs total (distributed primarily us-east/us-west/eu-central)

Supply notes / constraints:
- eu-central H100: vendor lead time 8–12 weeks; risk of slipping Mar/May tranches into Q3.
- ap-southeast H100: not planning adds in H1; treat as “select customers only” + cross-region failover for non-regulated tiers.

| Upside    | +16                | +32               | pull-forward H100 delivery; favorable spot procurement in us-west |

---

4) Headroom plan by tier (planning targets)

Interpretation:
- “Headroom” = extra capacity above forecasted committed demand, to protect throughput SLO floors under load variance, hot shards, and partial node loss.
- “Warm spares” = powered-on + ready nodes reserved for rapid failover / replacement; counted separately from headroom.

Target policy (proposed; pending SRE + Finance approval):

| Tier     | Planning headroom (above forecasted committed demand) | Warm spares posture | Notes |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------:|---------------------|------|
| Premium  | 25%                                                    | 1 node per region minimum (H100), plus 1 additional node per 10 Premium nodes | Designed for fastest restore + minimal SLO bleed |
| Plus     | 18%                                                    | 1 node per major region (us-east/us-west/eu-central) shared across Plus | Can borrow from burst reserve under control plane policy |
| Standard | 12%                                                    | none dedicated; relies on burst reserve + faster reprovisioning | Admission control more aggressive at saturation |

Burst reserve (separate from headroom):
- H100 reserve: 8–12% of committed H100 by region (target 10%); used for controlled burst + incident recovery.
- L40S reserve: 10–15% by region (target 12%); larger due to perf variance and workload burstiness.

Note to self (Jamal): align vocabulary between “headroom” here and Finance utilization assumptions; otherwise we double-count conservatism.

---

- Product tier packaging (in progress) increases conversion to Plus for customers requesting written throughput floors + defined burst.

We forecast “committed nodes” sold (8-GPU nodes) by tier, per region, by month.

5.2 Converting demand into GPU needs (rule-of-thumb)

Planned tier→shape mapping for forecasting (not contractual; for fleet math):
- Premium: 1 node = 8x H100
- Plus: 1 node = 8x H100 (preferred) OR 8x L40S for cost-sensitive customers with approved perf profile
- Standard: 1 node = 8x L40S (preferred) OR 8x A100 legacy where already deployed

For this forecast we assume:
- Premium: 100% H100
- Plus: 70% H100 / 30% L40S
- Standard: 80% L40S / 20% A100 (shrinks over time with retirements)

---

6) Capacity sufficiency check — H1 2026 (Base case)

6.1 Aggregate GPU demand from new sales (H1 totals)

From §5.1 (sum of new nodes by tier):
- Standard: 18 nodes
- Plus: 21 nodes
- Premium: 14 nodes
Total new nodes: 53

GPU equivalents (by assumption above):
- Premium: 14 nodes * 8 H100 = 112 H100 GPUs
- Plus: 21 nodes * 8 GPUs = 168 GPUs total; split -> ~118 H100 + ~50 L40S
- Standard: 18 nodes * 8 GPUs = 144 GPUs total; split -> ~115 L40S + ~29 A100

H1 new demand (approx):
- H100 GPUs: 112 + 118 = 230
- L40S GPUs: 50 + 115 = 165
- A100 GPUs: 29

Important: the above is *new bookings only*. We also have renewals/expansions on the existing base; those are modeled separately (see §6.2) as uplift, not as “new nodes sold”.

6.2 Existing base expansion + renewals uplift assumption

We apply an uplift factor to committed GPUs already deployed:
- us-east: +8% (mature base but steady expansion)
- us-west: +12% (more growth)
- eu-central: +15% (regulatory + larger initial footprints)
- eu-west: +6%
- ap-southeast: +10% (small base)

This uplift, when applied to starting fleet committed allocation (not shown in this sheet; pulled from fleet allocation dashboard weekly), is what drives “quiet” capacity pressure beyond net-new sales.

Action item: once ENG-19271 export is live, replace uplift heuristics with deployment-level forecast from quoting tool.

6.3 Can supply cover demand + headroom?

High-level conclusion (base case):
- H100: supply additions (+44) do not cover H1 net-new demand (230) by themselves; we rely on (a) converting a portion of Plus to L40S where acceptable, (b) keeping utilization within targets, and (c) not every “node sold” requiring net-new GPUs due to capacity already in warm/burst pools and contract start dates staggered.
- L40S: supply additions (+96) still likely tight if Standard conversion accelerates; however L40S is easier to source and can be flexed.
- A100: retirements (-48) require active migration plan; keep A100 only for pinned workloads and prevent new A100 commitments.

Translation: base-case is feasible only if:
1) We enforce tier→shape guardrails in quoting (Plus on L40S is allowed only with explicit perf profile acceptance), AND
2) We maintain the headroom policy without silently consuming it for planned launches.

---

7) Regional notes (what’s different by region)

us-east
- Most Premium demand; keep ≥2 warm spare H100 nodes at all times once Premium nodes >10.
- Networking bottleneck risk: watch east-1 rack-level oversubscription; Nina to confirm NIC profile for new H100 nodes.

us-west
- More bursty; expect higher variance in tokens/sec due to longer contexts and streaming.
- Recommendation: larger burst reserve on L40S (+3% over global target).

eu-central
- Highest procurement risk.
- Premium posture should be more conservative (consider 30% headroom if supply slips), otherwise we will page constantly.

ap-southeast
- Do not promise Premium unless we have confirmed H100 supply; steer to Plus on L40S with regional expectations.

---

8) Risks / mitigations (working list)

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
|------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| eu-central H100 delivery slips to Q3 | High | High | reserve overflow capacity in eu-west; steer some Plus to L40S; tighten Premium deal desk gating | Harish Reddy |
| Customer demand pulls forward (contracts start earlier) | Medium | High | enforce minimum lead times in order form; require ramp schedule for Premium | Vanessa Ortiz |
| Tier SLO definition increases effective headroom need | Medium | Medium/High | SRE to finalize exclusions + measurement window; recompute headroom after SLO semantics lock | Sean Gallagher |
| Streaming token accounting changes cause planning mismatch | Low/Medium | Medium | standardize metric pipeline + reconcile with billing export; validate against perf bench | Logan Wright |
| A100 retirements create stranded commitments | Medium | Medium | migration program + pricing incentives; hard stop on net-new A100 | Irene Choi |

---

9) Action items / next steps

- [Infra/Fleet] Confirm H100 purchase/lease plan and delivery dates by 2026-03-01 (eu-central prioritized). (Harish)
- [Capacity Planning] Replace uplift heuristic with deployment-level forecast once quoting export (ENG-19271) lands. (Jamal)
- [Product + Finance] Confirm acceptable Plus-on-L40S policy and discount guardrails so we can steer demand. (Lauren / Laura)
- [SRE] Lock headroom targets and warm spare posture assumptions; ensure not double-counted vs utilization targets. (Rafael / Sean)
- [Infra] Produce “regional capacity by tier” weekly snapshot for deal desk gating (simple CSV export until tooling is ready). (Vanessa)

---

Appendix A — Notes from procurement thread (informal)
- Vendor says eu-central H100 racks likely constrained by power + high competition; potential partial shipment.
- us-east supply looks stable; price pressure moderate.
- L40S: generally available; variability in node SKUs (CPU/RAM) may impact batching; keep node profiles consistent for Dedicated.

Appendix B — Open questions
1) Do we treat burst reserve as a paid add-on (customer) vs internal-only buffer? This changes whether we can “count it” in SLO protection.
2) How strict is Premium regional pinning (e.g., eu-central only)? If strict, our mitigation via eu-west overflow is limited.
3) For Plus, do we allow mixed-shape within a single customer deployment? (operationally complex; impacts how we count headroom).
